design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 of patient_balance_and_coverage_resolution (billing). Frozen 2026-09-22 10:40 EDT.

[Step 0 — snapshot, draw, claim]
draw_counts.py --task 1 printed: prerequisite_problems=1, problems=2, factor_counts=[4, 6]. Assignment: returned-payment replacement 4, credit refund 6 (root).
Occupied by task 0: billing_ext_card_on_file_charge, billing_ext_pre_placement_statement, billing_ext_final_notice_paydown and their tools (card-on-file charge, statement, final-notice paydown). Claimed here, disjoint from them: billing_ext_returned_payment_replacement (target pay_returned_payment_replacement_5bda38e8, owner=user) and billing_ext_credit_refund (target issue_credit_refund_942b7f9f, agent). After this task every extended policy of the difficulty is claimed exactly once; nothing is reserved.
Design thesis: surface goal "refund the duplicate imaging payment to my HSA card" -> prerequisite (a credit is refunded only after the charge whose check or ACH payment was most recently returned carries a card/HSA/cash payment posted after the return) -> core computation (credit balance with the plan add-back, less five amounts kept on the account) -> terminal state (a card replacement payment and a refund entry to the HSA card). Depth: one prerequisite hop the customer never mentions (she does not know her payments bounced). Breadth: 10 factors reading the ledger's return, fee, late-fee and correction history, the account's deductible/verification fields, and four other products (payplan plan status and missed installments, appointment bookings, membership billing cycle and dues, telehealth scheduled visits).
Scope rationale: a real returned-item control (no money leaves the practice while a returned check or ACH item stands unreplaced, so a bad check can never be refunded as a credit) makes the replacement a genuine prerequisite with a value effect: while the returned balances stand open they absorb the credit.

[Problem-tree card]
Root: billing_ext_credit_refund. Edge: credit refund -> returned-payment replacement, kind value_input, gate net_credit, form state. Prerequisite sentence (refund rule, affirmative direction, as a refunds desk states what a refund rests on): "A credit is refunded only after the charge whose check or ACH payment was most recently returned carries a card, HSA/FSA card or cash payment posted after that return." Four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; record-visible state (a payment entry of those methods on that charge, dated after the reversal); no tool, id or code token; exact scope (the charge of the most recent return, guaranteed-funds methods). Exactly one write of this difficulty posts a card payment against the charge a returned payment had paid: the returned-payment replacement, whose own rule says it "is posted as one card payment against the charge the most recently returned payment had paid". Derivation: sentence + ledger (latest reversal 2026-08-11 reverses the ACH payment on the coinsurance line of ENC-21741962; nothing posted on that line since) + the replacement rule -> make good the returned payments by card. Unresolved at opening: spec_return.txn_date = 2026-08-11, spec_ach.payment_method = ach, no later payment on spec_coi. Customer write: the replacement (owner=user; she pays with her own Visa on the secure line, the agent never handles card numbers). Load-bearing: skipping it gives a refund of 142.35 instead of 464.95. Topological order: replacement, then refund (unique). The persona never names the prerequisite; the tools validate nothing.
Charter direction mix across the difficulty: this sentence is affirmative ("only after"); task 0 carries one affirmative and one negated sentence.

[Base-invariant card]
Replacement writes billing_payment_posted, governed only by billing_payment_application; its designated_encounter gate is retired by the declared overwrite (the rule fixes the charge the replacement is posted against), so base_preconditions carry billing_payment_application as policy_scope. Refund writes billing_refund_issued, governed only by billing_credit_balance_refund: credit_hold_elapsed (time; anchor the posting date of the payment that created the credit, 2026-08-03 HSA card payment; Commercial PPO/POS credit_balance_hold_days 45 counted from the day after; the refund may be issued on the day the hold ends, 2026-09-17; just before: 2026-09-16 must wait; the handling date 2026-09-22 is past it), refund_once (no billing_refund_issued entry applies to that payment), refundable_status (status active). Declared overwrites of that policy: the "credit is applied to any other open charge" sentence (replaced by the plan-offset rule) and the "remaining credit ... is refunded" sentence (replaced by the order sentence with the amounts kept on the account).

[Business-object card]
Account bb910e69-20e5-4a9e-836c-e2c515df830f. Credit object: the imaging coinsurance line of ENC-21693127 (842.35) paid twice (card 2026-07-28 and HSA card 2026-08-03); the later payment created the credit and is the refund's object; refund method hsa_fsa_card (copied by the tool from that payment). Replacement object: the coinsurance line of ENC-21741962, whose ACH payment was the most recent return; the replacement covers both returns of the look-back (check 58.60 on ENC-21418806's deductible line, ACH 212.40), less the 18.40 correction on the ACH's charge, plus both 30.00 fees and the 10.00 late fee. Excluded from the offset: the plan-enrolled coinsurance of ENC-21602277 (remaining 486.68, active plan, no missed installment). Settled rows: copays collected at check-in, plan installments 1-4, monthly dues June-September, the first imaging payment.

[Factor card — returned-payment replacement (4; result 322.6)]
returned_scope (method): two returns in 12 months (restricted) -> both returns 271.00; baseline (most recent return only) -> 264.0. Near-misses: the check returned 2025-08-19 (and its 30.00 fee) lies 13 months back, outside the 12-month look-back and already made good by card on 2025-08-26; the card chargeback of 2026-06-24 on the Nurse Visit deductible (ENC-21480072) is a billing_payment_reversed row inside the 12 months but is neither a check nor an ACH return, so neither the scope, the fee count nor the restriction count takes it.
charge_reduction (parameter): 18.40 billing_error_correction on the ACH's charge -> 18.40 off; baseline -> 341.0.
returned_fee_inclusion (parameter): two fees in 12 months -> 60.00; baseline (latest fee only) -> 292.6.
late_fee_inclusion (parameter, multi-source): restricted and one late fee in 12 months -> 10.00; baseline -> 312.6.
Whole baseline: 242.4.

[Factor card — credit refund (6; result 464.95)]
plan_offset (method, cross-difficulty payplan, multi-source): active plan, installments paid and none missed in six months -> plan remaining 486.68 added back; baseline (every open charge absorbs the credit) -> 0.
booked_visit_hold (parameter, cross-difficulty appointment): Specialist Consultation booked 2026-10-06 -> 75.00 kept; baseline -> 539.95. Near-miss: completed imaging and procedure visits are not bookings.
returned_payment_reserve (parameter): two returns in 12 months -> 60.00 kept; baseline -> 524.95.
membership_dues_hold (parameter, cross-difficulty membership): monthly Essential membership, dues 79.00 kept; baseline -> 543.95.
deductible_reserve (parameter; both conditions are fields of the account row, not counted as multi-source): 118.40 remaining, verified 35 days ago -> min(118.40, 150.00) = 118.40 kept (the stale-verification tier would keep 150.00); baseline -> 583.35.
virtual_visit_hold (parameter, cross-difficulty telehealth): Specialty Video Follow-Up scheduled 2026-10-01 -> 45.00 kept; baseline -> 509.95.
Whole baseline: 355.67. Every factor sits off its fall-through tier; none reads an outcome stamp.

[Why initial_state rows exist]
Ledger rows reconcile the account to -33.07 at opening and carry: the credit (two imaging payments), both returns with their fees (restriction count, scope, reserve), the late fee (statement 2026-06-19 unpaid past its late-fee day; the 2026-07-28 payment was designated to the imaging encounter, not the statement), the correction (reduction factor), the plan installments and the enrolled charge (plan offset), copays and dues (reconciliation of the balance and the membership). Cross-product rows: payment plan and its ledger (active, no misses), appointments (four completed, one booked), the scheduled virtual visit, the monthly membership and its dues ledger. Automatic clauses checked: no statement was due after 2026-07-19 (the account has been in credit at every later cycle date); no late fee is owed for the 2026-07-19 statement (a payment of at least half of it came 2026-07-28); the plan's next installment falls due 2026-10-15; no collection or hold obligations.

[Persona design]
Evelyn Hartsock, friendly and organized, notebook-keeper. Volunteers only the surface goal (refund of the duplicate imaging payment to the HSA card) and the natural circumstance behind it (she paid on the portal, her husband paid again by phone with the HSA card), both entailed by the ledger. Gives name and phone to locate, DOB and SSN last four to verify when asked. Passive facts on request: bookings of Oct 6 and Oct 1, plan on autopay, monthly Essential membership. Passive reactions: agrees to make good bounced payments by card when the agent explains it and runs the handed-over payment with the agent's figures; accepts that part of the credit stays for upcoming visits or bills (asks once for a re-check); declines keeping the whole credit on the account; ends when the refund is confirmed. She never raises another ask and never supplies math.

[Standard solution and recomputation]
Reads: customer, identity, account, ledger, appointments, virtual visits, plan, plan ledger, membership, membership ledger. Writes: step 11 (handed over) pay_returned_payment_replacement_5bda38e8(account, ACH-returned coinsurance line, 322.6); step 13 issue_credit_refund_942b7f9f(account, 2026-08-03 HSA payment, 464.95).
Verification code: the authoring harness replays gold writes with the real tools on initial_state and evaluates each compute on the handling-time world through check_compute's build_env/eval_compute: replacement 322.6 (baseline 242.4); refund 464.95 (baseline 355.67; without the replacement 142.35).

[Draft recomputation from the visible context]
From the refund rule alone the agent learns that the refund waits on a guaranteed-funds payment after the latest return; the ledger shows the ACH return of 2026-08-11 with nothing after it; the replacement rule names the posting and the amount method; the refund rule then gives the add-back and the five amounts kept. The same 322.6 and 464.95 follow; the posting sentences fix both references; one reading remains: after step 11 the ACH-returned coinsurance line also carries more payment than its amount, but the rule counts only charges to which no returned check or ACH payment was ever applied, so the refund object and the credit-hold anchor stay the 2026-08-03 HSA payment.

[Closure]
returned-payment replacement -> pay_returned_payment_replacement_5bda38e8 -> computations[0] step 11 -> card payment entry on the returned charge; credit refund -> issue_credit_refund_942b7f9f -> computations[1] step 13 -> refund entry to hsa_fsa_card, credit reduced. charter_scope, required_documents and computations list the same two policies in the same order. One frozen_time; all writes synchronous.

[Difficulty-level closure]
Tasks 0 and 1 together claim all five extended policies and all five task tools, pairwise disjoint; every task has exactly its drawn prerequisite count and factor counts, at least one customer write, a multi-source and a cross-difficulty factor, and value_input edges on every prerequisite.


[Revision r2 — policy-task audit r1 closed item by item]
F-1: the replacement and refund now count only billing_payment_reversed rows whose payment_method is check or ach (compute and rule agree; the refund prerequisite condition names the latest check or ACH reversal). The new card chargeback on this world is the near-miss that shows it.
T1-F1 (no near-miss in the replacement): seeded two balance-neutral histories: a check returned 2025-08-19 with its fee, made good 2025-08-26 (outside the 12-month look-back, inside 24 months), and a card chargeback of 2026-06-24 on a Nurse Visit re-paid 2026-06-30 (inside the look-back but not a check/ACH return). Replacement stays 322.60; the near-misses are excluded by the rule's window and qualifier alone.
F-3 (two readings of the refund object after step 11): the refund rule now names the payment that created the credit as the most recently posted payment that brought the unreversed payments of a charge above its amount, counting only charges to which no returned check or ACH payment was ever applied, so the ACH-returned line (which the replacement overpays) is excluded; the object and the credit-hold anchor stay the 2026-08-03 HSA payment. The rule also now states the cash-to-check exception the tool applies (O-4).
T1-O2: deductible_remaining_usd is now 118.40, so the within-verification tier (lower of 118.40 and 150.00 = 118.40) differs from the stale tier (150.00); refund recomputed 464.95 (baseline 355.67; without the replacement 142.35).
T1-O3: deductible_reserve is no longer described as multi-source; the task's multi-source factors are plan_offset and late_fee_inclusion.
user_scenario:
You are Evelyn Hartsock, 50, a middle-school librarian from Westerville, Ohio, calling Linden Ridge Medical Group's Patient Services line from home on a Tuesday morning. You are friendly, organized and a little chatty, and you keep a notebook of household bills. Looking at the MyLinden portal you noticed that the bill for your June imaging was paid twice: you paid it yourself on the portal in late July, and your husband paid the same bill again over the phone in early August with your HSA card, not knowing you had already paid. You want the extra money refunded to the HSA card. That refund is the only thing you are calling about.
When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Evelyn Hartsock, and your phone number, 6145552743. To confirm your identity you give your date of birth, 1976-02-08, and the last four digits of your Social Security number, 2316, but only when the agent asks, one at a time. You do not know the exact amounts off-hand and you tell the agent to go by what the account shows.
Only if the agent asks about upcoming care: you have a cardiology consultation booked for October 6 and a video follow-up with urology scheduled for October 1. Only if asked about the payment plan for your spring procedure: it is on autopay and you believe every installment has gone through. Only if asked about the Linden membership: you have the Essential membership, billed monthly, since June.
If the agent explains that bank payments on your account that bounced have to be made good by card before any refund can go out, you are surprised, say your bank did change your checking account over the summer, and agree; when the agent hands you the secure payment step you complete it yourself with your Visa card, using the account, the charge reference and exactly the amount the agent gives you, and you read back the confirmation. If the agent tells you that part of the credit stays on the account for upcoming visits or bills, you accept that without arguing, though you ask them once to double-check the figure against the account. If the agent offers to keep the whole credit on the account instead of refunding it, you decline; you want the refund to the HSA card. Once the agent tells you the refund has been issued and to which card, you thank them and end the call.
